title: GREENER COMPOSITE STRUCTURES USING RECYCLABLE AND BIOBASED MATERIALS FOR OUT OF AUTOCLAVE PROCESS - EXPRO+
description: Objective:  To demonstrate the efficiency of sustainable and biobased resin to produce recyclable, repairable and reusable composite parts compliant with space requirement by out of autoclave process. Description:  The environmental impact of space activitiesis receiving increasing attention across the European space sector. In line with ESA's Ecodesign Policy, future missions are expected to assess their environmental footprint through Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) methodologies and identify solutions that reduce resource consumption, energy usage, waste generation, and hazardous materials. Composite manufacturing processes have been identifiedas a relevant environmental hotspot, notably during the preparation of the EcoStar IOD mission (ESA PrepE 24-P-M-OPS-12), where out-of-autoclave manufacturing using sustainable feedstocks was highlighted as a promising mitigation pathway. At this stage most of the resins are made using petroleum-based feedstock material and the market is mostly led by non-European large entities. Some of the chemical used to produce most of the resins (i.e Bisphenol A) are subject to increasing regulatory scrutiny and may face future restrictions under the European REACH framework, highlighting the need for sustainable and readily available alternative materials. In this work, sustainable European sourced feed stock material shall be used to produced thermosetting resin to be used in combination with carbon fibres to enable composite part manufacturing by out of autoclave process that will exhibit recyclable, repairable and reusable capabilities. This includes extended pot life resin, 100% biobased resin, REACH compliant resin and vitrimer-based resin. Composites based on carbon fibre will be produced using sustainable resin and tested to reach TRL 4 first at sample level and thenat breadboard level representative of existing mature design for space. The activity will also assess the environmental benefits of the proposed materials and processes through LCA, comparing them against conventional composite manufacturing approaches. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Review of the different out of autoclave processes existing for space applications, - - - - - - Review of the commercially available sustainable resins that could be used for out of autoclave processes, Performing a trade-off taking into account materials/processes compatibility, sustainability aspect of the resin, capability to enable composite recycling, reuse and repairability Select at least 2 different out of autoclave processes for further investigation, Development of test plan at sample level to assess the performance of the chosen material and process, Design, produce and test 2 demonstrators based on relevant composite parts for space applications, Perform simplified LCA and Ecodesign trade off and selection.Deliverables:Breadboard, Report

description: Objective:To develop and assess quantum computing algorithms, methods and related tools for solving specific spacerelated computational challenges with higher performance and reliability than the state of the art achieved with the classical technologies.Description:Quantum computing technologies are progressing rapidly, with early-stage commercial and academicplatforms offering capabilities relevant to space applications. As one of the strategic sectors expected to benefit from quantum advantage, the space domain offers complex, high-impact challenges that can guide algorithm development and platform requirements. Lessons learned from these applications will be transferable to other sectors, enabling a broader quantum technology ecosystem. This activity aims to ensure European industry is quantum-ready and positioned to lead in the global race for space-enabled quantum technologies. It supports European strategic autonomy by fostering sovereign capabilities in quantum algorithm development, hybrid integration, and secure processing architectures tailored to ESA or national mission needs. The initiative also strengthens Europe's industrial competitiveness by enabling use-case-driven innovation and demonstrating technical leadership in both terrestrial and space environments. This activity aimsto encourage the usage of quantum computing potentials to address the challenges in space missions and technologies. title: T811-902SD ADVANCED IN-SITU DATA PROCESSING FOR SPACE DEBRIS MODEL VALIDATION (EXPRO+)
description: The knowledge on the small space debris population is still limited. Large debris populations are welldocumented,with ground radarand telescopes cataloguing objects >10 cm in Low Earth Orbit and 30-40 cmin Geostationary Orbit. Debris in the cm to sub-cm range remains largely uncharted, relying on statisticalsampling via remote sensing, in-situ detectors and retrieved space-exposed hardware. Due to their highvelocities, small debris impacts are a threat to sensitive spacecraft equipment (panels, de-orbitingmechanisms,exposed payloads) and human life. Space debris models, used for risk assessment, rely oncollected samples to model small debris.Several recent space missions carried detectors, with data being collected more often than before. However,there is still no unifiedway to neither collect nor process these efficiently for the output quantities (flux, objectmass/diameter, velocity, source) to beincluded in a model. With the advances in technology and big datahandling, acquisition, storing and efficient processing becomes more realistic.This activity aims to develop a software that can ingest, store and process in-situ measurements of spacedebris. Itwill produce quantities that can be ingested without modifications in the validation toolchain of a spacedebris model. The measurements should include in-situ impact datasets, focusing on the widely usedpiezoelectric and plasma detectors. The inclusion of in-situoptical data and data from photographic surveyswill be considered.
